memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If your grain offering is cooked in a pan, it is to be made of the finest flour and some olive oil. Bring the grain offering made of these things to the LORD; present it to the priest, who shall take it to the altar.'" - Lev 2:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three verses in a row have described the same offering prepared three different ways: in an oven, on a griddle, in a pan. God has now spelled out every cooking method an ordinary Israelite kitchen might have.

Why so much detail about pots and pans?

Because God was making sure no one was excluded by their circumstances. Some families had access to an oven. Some had only a flat griddle over a fire. Some had a simple pan. God named every one of them so that no woman kneading dough in a tent could think, my method is not good enough for God.

This is the same pastoral heart we saw in chapter 1, where the offering scaled from bull to bird. God keeps making room.

And note the movement in verse 8: bring it, present it to the priest, and the priest takes it to the altar. The worshipper could not place his own gift on the altar. It had to pass through appointed hands. Our worship still reaches the Father through a Mediator — we offer a sacrifice of praise to God through Jesus (Heb 13:15). It is His hands that carry our imperfect offerings to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I ever felt my circumstances make my worship less acceptable to God?
2. What does it mean to me that Christ carries my worship to the Father?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You made room for every kind of worshipper. Carry my offering to the Father through Christ, and let it be received. Amen.
